question.text: Under SEBI (AIF) Regulations and PIT Regulations, Category I Venture Capital Funds, SME Funds and Category II AIFs enjoy a specific exemption from certain PIT provisions when investing in SME-listed companies pursuant to due diligence, subject to conditions. Which of the following conditions apply?

answer.text: Fund must disclose the due-diligence trade to the stock exchange where the investee is listed within two trading days; such investment is locked-in for 1 year from date of investment
No disclosure is needed; lock-in is 6 months
The exemption applies only to buy-side trades, not sell-side
Only Cat III AIFs are eligible for this carve-out

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 4(b)(i)(b)/(ii) carve-outs in SEBI (AIF) Regulations read with PIT Regulations 3(1), 3(2), and 4(1): VCFs, SME Funds, and Cat II AIFs are exempt from the specified PIT sub-regulations for SME-exchange investments made pursuant to due-diligence, subject to: (a) disclosure of the trade to the stock exchange within 2 trading days; (b) 1-year lock-in from date of investment. The Trap: Option B drops the disclosure requirement. Option C narrows scope to buy-only. Option D wrongly identifies Cat III (PIT carve-out is Cat I VCF/SME/Cat II). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C uniquely tests the PIT SME carve-out. XV (RA) touches this tangentially.
